column1: # Fukazawa Y., Betoya-Nonesa J. G., Pu J., Ohto A., Kawano N., 2006, ApJ 636, 698, 'Scaling Mass Profiles around Elliptical Galaxies Observed with Chandra and XMM-Newton'
# Transcribed by transcribe_fukazawa.py from ms.tex in the tarball (1626 lines); run log transcribe_fukazawa.out

# Table 4 = deluxetable 'table:results' (4th of 5 in order of appearance), caption line 1492, data lines 1506-1558: Galaxy, kT_i, kT_o, n_t-r, n_beta, n_depro, R_max, M/L_B, n_e,10kpc, type. ALL 53 rows.

# D_Mpc = Table 1 = deluxetable 'tab:sample-chandra', caption line 1309, data lines 1322-1375; note b: 'D is a distance to the galaxy ... taken from O'Sullivan et al. (2001) [MNRAS 328, 461] and NED'.
# Distance convention: 'Throughout this paper, we assume H0=70 km/s/Mpc' (ms.tex line 261); the analysis uses the Table 1 D (many Virgo galaxies at 15.9 Mpc; lines 686-689: NGC 4697 at 15.1 Mpc).

# ne10_1e-3cm3 = 'the hot gas electron density at 10 kpc' (note f), from the beta-model fit to the 0.5-1.5 keV surface brightness (Sec. 3.2); NO per-galaxy error is given (text: beta fits to <10%, local structure 'gives 10% error to the hot gas density'); nan = '---' (VCXG: emission inside 10 kpc).

# n_beta = number of beta components fitted to the surface brightness (the AGN component not counted). Rmax_kpc = 'maximum detection radius (kpc)'; Rmax_lower_limit = 1 where printed as '>' (emission beyond the field edge: every such row gives R_max/D = 397-399 arcsec on ACIS-S, 713-737 on ACIS-I).
